messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] stepwiseqtl() for traits with bi-modal distribution
parts:
I'd start with just doing QTL mapping with the trait as is, hoping to find a QTL which explains the two modes. Or, I might turn it into a binary trait, splitting at 0.0025, again to look for a locus that explains the two modes.

karl


On Aug 14, 2012, at 5:03 AM, matthieu BOGARD wrote:

> Dear Pr Broman,
>
> I'm currently analysing a trait which distribution is clearly bi-modal (see the .pdf attached). As far as I understand, this case is intermediate between the "two-part" model and the "binay" model available in scanone().
>
> I could presumably analyse separately the two modes but - leaving aside the problem of determining a threshold to separate the two modes- this might reduce the statistical power as the number of individuals per mode would be reduced. Moreover, this would lead to miss the major gene behind this bi-modal distribution.
>
> What model/startegy would you recommend in that particular case ?
>
> Regards,
> Matthieu
